Question for today: where does CellCo lose most of its output, and what is fixing it worth in the production plan?

## Four ways to count quality {#metrics}

```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Metric</th><th>Definition</th><th>CellCo, one week</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>First-pass yield (FPY)</td><td>Share of units passing a step the first time, without rework</td><td>Coating 0.972, slitting 0.981, assembly 0.967, formation and aging test 0.874 (Block 1: 0.95 × 0.92)</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Rolled throughput yield (RTY)</td><td>Product of the FPYs: share passing every step first time</td><td class="hit">0.972 × 0.981 × 0.967 × 0.874 = 0.806</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Defects per million opportunities (DPMO)</td><td>Defects ÷ (units × opportunities per unit) × 10<sup>6</sup></td><td>2,900 ÷ (37,260 × 10) × 10<sup>6</sup> = 7,780</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Overall equipment effectiveness (OEE)</td><td>Availability × performance × quality</td><td>Computed in the activity</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

::: {.bridge}
In Block 1, the formation and aging stage passed **0.874** of cells first time but ended with **0.933** good after rework. The 5.9-point gap is the hidden factory: cells that pass only after rework, using test time and capacity that the final yield does not show.
:::

## OEE: one number, three losses {#oee}

::: {.two}
::: {}
**Availability** = run time ÷ planned time. Lost to breakdowns, die changes, waiting for material.

**Performance** = actual output ÷ (run time × ideal rate). Lost to minor stops and reduced speed.

**Quality** = good first-pass output ÷ actual output. Lost to scrap and rework.
:::
::: {}
::: {.route-question}
Breakdowns and scrap are logged; minor stops and slow running often are not. OEE makes the unlogged losses visible by working back from the ideal rate.
:::
[World-class OEE is often quoted near 85%. Compare a line with its own history rather than with that figure.]{.hint}
:::
:::

## Activity · Answer {#act1-answer data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="widget" id="oex">
  <div class="w-controls">
    <label class="w-slider">Die changes, h <strong id="oex-dv">9</strong><input type="range" id="oex-d" min="0" max="20" step="1" value="9"></label>
    <label class="w-slider">Cells made <strong id="oex-mv">37,260</strong><input type="range" id="oex-m" min="30000" max="45000" step="60" value="37260"></label>
    <label class="w-slider">Good first time, % <strong id="oex-qv">97.2</strong><input type="range" id="oex-q" min="85" max="99.5" step="0.01" value="97.198"></label>
  </div>
  <svg id="oex-svg" viewBox="0 0 1160 230" role="img" aria-label="Weekly losses in cells, largest first"></svg>
  <div class="w-readout" id="oex-out" aria-live="polite"></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('oex'); if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  function draw() {
    const die = +document.getElementById('oex-d').value, run = 160 - die - 8 - 5;
    const made = Math.min(+document.getElementById('oex-m').value, Math.floor(run * 300)), q = +document.getElementById('oex-q').value / 100, good = Math.round(made * q);
    document.getElementById('oex-dv').textContent = die; document.getElementById('oex-mv').textContent = made.toLocaleString('en-US'); document.getElementById('oex-qv').textContent = (100 * q).toFixed(1);
    const A = run / 160, P = made / (run * 300), Q = good / made;
    const loss = [['Minor stops and slow running', run * 300 - made], ['Scrap and rework', made - good], ['Die changes', die * 300], ['Breakdowns', 8 * 300], ['Waiting for material', 5 * 300]].sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1]);
    const W = 1160, L = 300, R = 120, mx = Math.max(6000, loss[0][1]), X = (v) => L + v / mx * (W - L - R);
    let g = '';
    loss.forEach(([n, v], i) => { const y = 14 + i * 42; g += `<text x="${L - 12}" y="${y + 22}" text-anchor="end" font-size="17" fill="#1C242B">${n}</text><rect x="${L}" y="${y}" width="${X(v) - L}" height="30" fill="${i === 0 ? '#E29A2D' : '#0F6E6B'}"/><text x="${X(v) + 8}" y="${y + 22}" font-size="17" fill="#333F4A">${Math.round(v).toLocaleString('en-US')} cells</text>`; });
    document.getElementById('oex-svg').innerHTML = g;
    document.getElementById('oex-out').innerHTML = `Availability ${(100 * A).toFixed(1)}%, performance ${(100 * P).toFixed(1)}%, quality ${(100 * Q).toFixed(1)}%: <span class="best">OEE ${(100 * A * P * Q).toFixed(1)}%</span>. Largest single loss: ${loss[0][0].toLowerCase()}.`;
  }
  root.addEventListener('input', draw);
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

[Last week: availability 86.3%, performance 90.0%, quality 97.2% (the coating FPY), OEE 75.5%. The largest single loss, 4,140 cells, is the one nobody logs: minor stops and slow running.]{.hint}

## From yield to profit {#yield-profit data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="widget" id="ypx">
  <div class="w-controls"><label class="w-slider">Coating first-pass yield <strong id="ypx-v">0.972</strong><input type="range" id="ypx-y" min="0.972" max="0.995" step="0.001" value="0.986"></label></div>
  <div class="w-readout" id="ypx-out" aria-live="polite"></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('ypx'); if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  function draw() {
    const y = +document.getElementById('ypx-y').value; document.getElementById('ypx-v').textContent = y.toFixed(3);
    const hrs = 240 * (y / 0.972 - 1), eff = 240 + hrs, gain = 15 * Math.min(hrs, 60), rty = 0.806 * y / 0.972;
    document.getElementById('ypx-out').innerHTML = `RTY rises from 0.806 to <b>${rty.toFixed(3)}</b>. The same 240 coating hours now make as much good output as <b>${eff.toFixed(1)} hours</b> did before: ${hrs.toFixed(1)} extra effective hours, worth <span class="best">CNY ${gain.toFixed(0)} thousand a week</span>, about CNY ${(gain * 52 / 1000).toFixed(1)} million a year, at the shadow price of 15 per hour${hrs > 60 ? ' (capped: above 300 hours formation binds)' : ''}.`;
  }
  document.getElementById('ypx-y').addEventListener('input', draw);
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

::: {.two}
::: {}
**The link to the LP.** Coating is CellCo's bottleneck. Any coating loss removed acts like extra coating hours, priced by the shadow price from Session 12: CNY 15,000 per hour up to 300 hours.
:::
::: {}
**Where the yield is.** Halving coating defects (FPY 0.972 to 0.986) is worth about CNY 52,000 a week. The mass-loading work in Session 17 removes only about 700 ppm; most coating losses are streaks, pinholes and edges. The Pareto, not one capability index, shows where the yield is.
:::
:::

```{=html}
    <tr><td>Markov Analysis</td><td>How do yield and maintenance behave?</td><td>Yield from formation 0.933; preventive maintenance only in Major wear</td></tr>

    <tr><td>Linear Programming</td><td>What to make each week?</td><td>E 30, P 60 MWh; a coating hour is worth CNY 15,000</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Quality Control</td><td>Is the coating in control and capable?</td><td>In control; C<sub>pk</sub> 1.07, 1.33 needs re-centering and σ 0.150</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

::: {.bridge}
Each method answered one question well and none answered all of them. The decisions improved where one module's output became another's input: the yield fed the LP, the shadow price priced the quality project.
:::

## What we learned {#debrief}

::: {.takeaways}
::: {.tk}
RTY counts first-pass quality across steps; the gap to final yield is the hidden factory of rework.
:::
::: {.tk}
OEE exposes unlogged losses. CellCo's largest single loss is minor stops and slow running, not scrap.
:::
::: {.tk .key}
At the bottleneck, a yield gain is a capacity gain, priced by the LP's shadow price.
:::
:::

[Thank you for your work in both blocks.]{.note-line}
